qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Canadian Big Six oligopoly protected by OSFI regulatory charter barriers and sticky low-cost core deposit franchise. High domestic market share in residential mortgages, personal banking, and commercial lending. Primary erosion risks: elevated concentration in Canadian residential real estate mortgages during housing downturns, US commercial real estate credit exposure, fintech payment disintermediation, and macro rate fluctuations.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (REJECT). While CIBC holds an entrenched position within Canada's Big Six banking oligopoly with strong domestic execution and multi-cycle ROE of 13-16%, as a fractional-reserve commercial deposit-taking bank it structurally fails the Munger Gate 6 peace-of-mind solvency standard. Operating at ~16x asset/equity leverage and heavily exposed to domestic residential mortgages, its balance sheet inherently relies on depositor confidence and central bank/CDIC liquidity backstops ('kindness of strangers').
qualitative.evidence: Canadian Big Six chartered bank with significant market share in Canadian retail banking, wealth management, and residential mortgages. Historical 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 27.1% with multi-cycle ROE around 14-15%. However, Gate 6 structural rejection is absolute for commercial deposit banks: balance sheet carries over C$1.0T in assets against ~C$64B in common equity (>15-16x leverage) and C$140.9B in long-term debt liabilities. The institution relies on short-term demand deposits and wholesale credit facilities to fund long-term mortgages and loans, subjecting equity to asset-liability duration mismatch and credit cycle tail risk.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
